stories.title: A hidden “on switch” in human DNA has finally been decoded
stories.simple_summary: Scientists have figured out how to read an important switch in your DNA that turns genes on and off. This is a basic science discovery about how our bodies work.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly for medical researchers right now — it may help treat diseases someday, but there's nothing you need to do about it today.

stories.title: Does this image show creepy 'spider' on Mars?
stories.simple_summary: Someone shared a strange-looking image that looked like a spider on Mars, and Snopes (a fact-checking website) looked into whether it's real. It's probably just a rock formation that looks spider-like.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you — it's just a fun internet mystery.

stories.title: Dr. Dre Says He Uses AI to Produce Songs
stories.simple_summary: Music producer Dr. Dre says he uses AI computer tools to help make songs. AI can now create music sounds and help with production.
stories.why_it_matters: If you enjoy music, AI is changing how some songs get made — but most music still comes from human artists and producers.

stories.title: Who’s behind the new ‘stealth model’ Ox Alpha?
stories.simple_summary: A new AI system called Ox Alpha has appeared online and nobody publicly knows who created it, which has made some people curious and excited about it.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly interesting to AI fans and investors — nothing that affects your daily life.

stories.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
stories.simple_summary: A company called Linkdaze made a smart calendar that uses AI to help you plan meals and organize your household without charging extra money for those features.
stories.why_it_matters: If you struggle with meal planning or keeping track of family schedules, this is a free tool worth trying.

stories.title: ‘We are hitting a different chapter’: OpenAI leader warns of threat of ‘persistent’ AI cyber-attacks
stories.simple_summary: The leader of OpenAI (a big AI company) warned that hackers are using AI to attack computers and networks in new ways that are harder to stop.
stories.why_it_matters: Computer security is getting trickier — make sure your passwords are strong and be extra careful about emails asking for personal information.

stories.title: Billionaires Stanley Druckenmiller and Dan Loeb Both Sold Broadcom and Piled Into This Virtual Monopoly Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Instead
stories.simple_summary: Some very rich investors sold their shares in one computer company and bought shares in AI companies instead, betting that AI stocks will do well.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors with stock portfolios — nothing you need to act on unless you're managing investment money.

stories.title: Wyoming Police Departments Testing AI To Generate Reports, Look At Evidence
stories.simple_summary: Police departments in Wyoming are testing AI tools to write up police reports and analyze evidence from crime scenes automatically.
stories.why_it_matters: This could make police reports faster and more consistent, but it's still being tested and may not reach most departments soon.

stories.title: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
stories.simple_summary: Flock Safety is a company that makes cameras for tracking cars and solving crimes, but many people are worried these cameras could be misused to watch innocent people without permission.
stories.why_it_matters: If you care about privacy, this is worth knowing about — these cameras are being used in some neighborhoods, so ask your local police if they use this system.

stories.title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
stories.simple_summary: AI systems were trained by using millions of copyrighted books without asking authors first, and now authors are questioning whether that's legal. The answer is complicated and still being debated in court.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're a writer or artist, this matters because AI is using your work without paying you — if you're not, it mostly affects what content creators earn.

stories.title: Nvidia’s 15% Price Hike Reveals the Hidden Cost of the AI Boom
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia, a company that makes computer chips for AI, raised its prices by 15%, which means AI products will get more expensive for everyone who buys them.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important to investors and tech companies building AI — it may slowly increase prices of AI services, but probably not immediately.

stories.title: Why is AI going on a hacking spree?
stories.simple_summary: AI systems are being used by hackers to attack computers and break into networks more effectively than before.
stories.why_it_matters: Use strong passwords and watch for suspicious emails — hackers' tools are improving, so your caution needs to stay sharp.
